defects.description: `abs(n)` is computed but its result is discarded (not assigned back to `n`), so negative inputs are never made positive and the loop returns 0 for them.
paraphrases: The line should be `n = abs(n)`; as written the absolute value is thrown away.
Negative numbers are not normalized because the `abs(n)` result is not stored.
`sum_of_digits(-123)` returns 0 instead of 6 since `n` stays negative.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `n = abs(n)`. Real (negatives handled wrong), findable via the docstring example for -123, distinct.

defects.description: The digit is extracted with integer division (`n // 10`) instead of the remainder (`n % 10`), so it adds the truncated quotient rather than the last digit.
paraphrases: `res += n // 10` should be `res += n % 10`; it accumulates the wrong quantity.
The last digit is obtained with `% 10`, not `// 10`.
Using `//` sums quotients instead of digits, so `sum_of_digits(123)` is not 6.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `res += n % 10`. Real (wrong sum), findable via the docstring examples, distinct from the shift on the next line.

defects.description: The loop condition is `while n > 1`, which stops before processing the final (most significant) digit; it should be `while n > 0`.
paraphrases: `while n > 1` drops the last digit; the loop should run `while n > 0`.
The leading digit is never added because the loop exits one iteration early.
Off-by-one loop bound: it terminates at n == 1 instead of n == 0.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `while n > 0:`. Real (drops the most significant digit), findable via the docstring examples, distinct.
